Pause motion, then switch methods to compare the same pose in the same place.

Nearest, bilinear, trilinear and supported anisotropic modes use the GPU texture sampler. Trilinear and anisotropic use separate mipmapped textures per swim frame. Cubic sharpness adjusts the Catmull–Rom family (B=0); only C=0.50 is standard Catmull–Rom. Limit halos confines the result to the central 2×2 texel color/alpha range, which may reduce crispness. These controls do not increase the 16 texture lookups, but the limiter adds arithmetic. Bicubic modes use custom shaders; Catmull–Rom is sharper, Mitchell more balanced, B-spline softer. Filter amount applies only to Adjustable blend. Reduce Fish size to compare minification; anisotropic filtering may resemble trilinear on these flat sprites. Edge-only smoothing blends where the texture has transparency, preserving fully opaque interior detail; transparent holes are smoothed too. RotSprite-style remains available in Experiment. All methods use the same motion and angles. These are visual experiments; full-tank performance has not been measured. The tank itself is unchanged.
